text: Debugging is a crucial skill for any programmer. When a program doesn't work as expected, the first step is to identify the bug clearly. Instead of guessing, a systematic approach works best: reproduce the problem, then narrow down the possible causes step by step. Modern debugging tools, such as breakpoints and step-through execution, allow you to pause the code and inspect its state at any moment. Logging is another powerful method—adding print statements or log messages helps you trace the flow of data and see where things go wrong. By combining these techniques, you can solve even the trickiest issues without frustration.
